title: Needed Research documents record known gaps inside the rulebook rather than outside it
content:
A.1.2.2.2.30 defines the Needed Research Type, whose single component is a Research Prompt describing "potential problems, unanswered questions or other concerns associated with the Target Document" — gaps or conflicts in logic, or operational questions "to which there are currently no answers."

The addressing scheme is the tell. Alone among Supporting Documents, Needed Research "is not derived from the Supporting Root of their Target Document"; identifiers are standalone, prefixed "NR-" plus an incremented number. The stated reason: this "enables them to be linked to more than one Atlas Document, no matter the latter's location in the Atlas document tree."

That break from the hierarchy is necessary because real gaps are cross-cutting. A missing evidentiary standard or an unresolved role-conflict question does not belong to one branch, and forcing it into one would fragment it into duplicates that each get partially answered. Giving research needs their own namespace lets a single open question be the shared referent for every document it touches.

The governance significance is that a framework which asserts its own supremacy and permanence also ships a **public, addressable list of what it does not yet know**. A.1.2.2.2.30 opens submission to "the Core Facilitator, Atlas workstream contributors or other ecosystem participants," processed "through the standardized Atlas data integration protocol." Doubt has a filing location and a queue, which is what stops unresolved problems from being resolved informally by whoever is acting under pressure.

A.1.2.2.2.30 also notes these are most effective attached to Primary or Supporting Documents rather than the abstract Immutable layers, because it is at the concrete layer that the abstract logic actually has to be turned into an actionable rule — so that is where its gaps become visible.
description: The NR- prefix gives them standalone identifiers so one research need can attach to multiple Atlas Documents anywhere in the tree, and any participant may submit inputs.
